slots.title: October CPI due at 8:30 with 3.9% YoY est.
slots.body:
October CPI drops at 8:30 a.m.
ET — the main gauge of how fast everyday prices are rising.

Economists expect:
- Inflation rate YoY (Oct): 3.9% vs 3.7% prior
- Inflation rate MoM (Oct): 0.3% vs 0.6% prior
- Core inflation YoY (Oct): 2.8% vs 2.6% prior — “core” strips out volatile food and energy
- Core inflation MoM (Oct): 0.2% est. vs 0.3% prior

CPI s.a index level est.: 337 vs 336.3 prior.

NFIB small-business optimism (Oct) is also on the calendar at 11:00 a.m., est. 97.7 vs 97.9 prior — lower impact.

Prior session, $^GSPC +2.3% to 7,549.94 and $^VIX -22.3% to 19.92 ahead of the print.

What number on core YoY are you watching first?

slots.title: Oil slips after Trump plays down Iran risk
slots.body:
Energy sold off into the U.S. open narrative.

- $USO (oil fund proxy): -3.9% to 142.66
- Brent crude ($BZUSD): -1.0% to 91.69

WSJ and Reuters tied the move to oil weakening after President Trump played down the prospect of further U.S. strikes on Iran.

Separately, Reuters reported Hormuz LNG traffic hit its highest October level since the Iran war began — tanker flows vs strike headlines sitting in the same news cycle.

Gold $GCUSD: +0.4% to 4,132.70 on the day in the cross-asset snapshot.

slots.title: China exports +35.2%, beat 33.5% poll
slots.body:
China’s October trade print landed ahead of expectations.

Goods exports: +35.2% YoY in October.

That beat the +33.5% jump economists polled by Reuters had expected.

September’s pace was +36.3% YoY — so growth stayed strong but slowed slightly month to month.

CNBC also noted imports surged past expectations and the trade surplus narrowed sharply — detail in the full release coverage.

Overnight equities:
- Hang Seng $^HSI: +0.5% to 24,574.00
- Nikkei $^N225: +3.2% to 60,636.66

U.S. indexes finished higher into this data week: $^IXIC +2.7% to 25,253.14.

Which China line item matters more for your read — exports, imports, or the surplus?

slots.title: US Cash Session — Nov. 10, 2026
slots.body:
U.S. equities finished broadly higher.
The S&P 500 rose 2.3% to 7,549.94 (+173.08 points).
The Nasdaq Composite gained 2.7% to 25,253.14 and the Dow added 2.2% to 52,389.75 (+1,104.02 points).
The Russell 2000 led among the benchmarks shown, up 3.1% to 2,840.81.

Implied volatility collapsed alongside the rally: the VIX fell 22.3% to 19.92 from 25.64, with an intraday low of 19.64.

October consumer inflation releases were on the U.S. economic calendar for 8:30 a.m.
ET (headline and core year-over-year and month-over-month measures, plus the CPI index level).
The injected session bundle lists estimates and prior readings only, not released actuals for that print.

Across Nasdaq-classified sectors, utilities averaged +3.6%, industrials +3.2%, technology +2.7%, consumer defensive +1.4%, real estate +1.4%, healthcare +1.1%, consumer cyclical +1.2%, basic materials +0.8%, energy +0.2%, communication services +0.1%, and financial services -0.1%.

Mega-cap technology was mixed despite the index gains.
AMD rose 13.3% to 508.58; Broadcom rose 8.8% to 319.48.
NVIDIA fell 4.3% to 178.67 and was among the most active symbols in the session list.
Microsoft rose 2.7% to 545.18, Apple 2.4% to 350.69, Amazon 2.9% to 266.93, and Tesla 5.5% to 378.05.
Alibaba slipped 3.7% to 105.36.

Several names on the earnings calendar for Nov. 10 showed post-close prices in the data: TransDigm ($TDG) +1.8% to 1,218.85, Venture Global ($VG) +2.4% to 11.80, CoreWeave ($CRWV) +5.6% to 48.98, Scholar Rock ($SRRK) +9.8% to 51.55, and Veradermics ($MANE) +3.7% to 143.95.
EPS estimates were on the calendar; actual reported EPS figures were not in the injected close bundle.

Oil and energy equities diverged from the equity rally.
Brent crude was down 1.0% to 91.66; the United States Oil Fund ($USO) fell 3.9% to 142.66.
Chevron ($CVX) edged down 0.9% to 210.78.
Headlines in the feed tied weaker crude to eased concern over escalation in U.S.–Iran tension.

Gold futures ($GCUSD) rose 0.4% to 4,132.60.
The Invesco dollar bull ETF ($UUP) slipped 0.5% to 28.97.
Bitcoin ($BTCUSD) was down 0.6% to 74,765.91.

Overseas indexes in the bundle were mostly firm: Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose 3.2% to 60,658.68; Germany exposure via $EWG gained 3.4% to 42.99; the FTSE 100 added 1.0% to 10,782.87; the Hang Seng rose 0.4% to 24,558.50.

Treasury yields in the snapshot dated 2026-11-06 showed the 10-year at 4.9% and a 2s10s spread of 0.35 percentage points; that file was not stamped for the Nov. 10 cash close.

High-beta single names in the liquid gainers screen included Delcath ($DCTH) +35.8%, MindForge ($MF) +34.7%, and United-Guardian ($UG) +31.9%.
Janux Therapeutics ($JANX) led liquid losers at -27.6% to 12.76.
